  "required_fixes": [
    "RF01 (P1) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/learner_domain.rs:876–882 performs an unscoped learner-namespace purge after awaiting the old session's revocation. SignOutAcademy publishes SignedOut immediately, and StartAcademySignIn can admit a new flow before that cleanup finishes (authority.rs:1568–1623). If A's revocation is delayed and B signs in, A's eventual purge deletes B's newly saved refresh token while B remains displayed as signed in. A related path exists at learner_domain.rs:789–817: a cancelled Completing flow can return from desktop.me, purge the namespace and write its old grant before checking its flow number at commit, deleting a newer flow's credential. Make asynchronous credential effects generation-owned and ensure obsolete work cannot purge or replace a newer session's records. Acceptance: barrier-controlled production-interface tests delaying A's revocation, and separately A's desktop.me/credential write, while B completes sign-in; releasing A must preserve B's record and restart usability, revoke/delete only A's grant, and never revive A.",
    "RF02 (P1) — learner_domain.rs:254–281 and 789–817 write refresh-token records before establishing durable ownership. Rotation treats save_with(...).is_ok() as a durable commit, although save_with accepts StoreError::Unconfirmed; it then deletes the old record. A crash can therefore restore a document pointing to the deleted old record while leaving the new live refresh token untracked. A crash between the initial sign-in put and document save similarly leaves an untracked credential. Delete/purge failures are ignored, with no durable learner cleanup ledger or startup recovery. Reset also waits only for scan writes_in_flight (authority.rs:1787–1802), so an outstanding learner put can land after the learner namespace was purged. Extend the protected-storage transaction/recovery discipline to namespace-aware learner writes, rotations and cleanup; do not retire the previous record on an unconfirmed ownership transfer, and coordinate reset with admitted learner writes. Acceptance: visible-versus-durable ScriptedStore crash tests at put/save/delete boundaries, Unconfirmed rotation, failed cleanup followed by restart, and reset with a held learner put. Every retained token must have durable ownership or recoverable cleanup, with no post-reset orphan and truthful failure state.",
    "RF03 (P2) — crates/desktop-core/src/academy.rs:510–517 returns an error envelope directly, while the private-assessment-field screen runs only on successful result.data at line 527. Thus a valid non-2xx tRPC error containing error.json.data.answerKey, rubric, serverSpec or another protected field bypasses the same boundary that rejects those fields in successful replies; desktop-link forwards that error through transformResult into TRPCClientError.data. Screen or safely project all renderer-visible envelope branches while preserving legitimate learner domain errors. Acceptance: literal 400/500 error fixtures with nested protected fields must be refused or sanitized before IPC and remain absent from the production tRPC client's errors; ordinary domainCode/error fixtures must retain their intended behavior.",
    "RF04 (P2) — apps/desktop/src/features/academy/desktop-link.ts:91–102 discards result.outcome. An admitted mutation that fails with Outcome::Unknown becomes 'Academy could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.' with no structured remote outcome. I reproduced this by executing the production link in memory with a synthetic native failed/network/unknown result: TRPCClientError.data contained only code, httpStatus and desktop. CallReply::Error/AcademyCallResult::Error also drops the runtime's Unknown distinction for HTTP 5xx. Preserve the native remote outcome through the tRPC error interface and distinguish a possibly completed mutation from NotSent/Rejected, including admission/observation uncertainty. Acceptance: production-link tests for a mutation whose reply is lost, timeout/cancellation after dispatch and HTTP 5xx must expose Unknown with possible-effect guidance, retain NotSent/Rejected distinctions, and send no automatic second mutation."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [],
  "optional_suggestions": [],
  "limitations": [
    "I independently recomputed all four supplied fingerprints and verified all 22 packet references, recorded tool binaries, command-log hashes and fixture executable/bundle. C03 and P01 receipt/request/verdict/raw-output hashes, completion entries and commit ancestry agree. Retained-byte consistency is not proof of provider authorship.",
    "I independently ran the existing academy_identity executable against in-memory stores and synthetic loopback TLS: all 15 tests passed. I also executed the production TypeScript link in memory with a synthetic native result to confirm RF04. RF01–RF03 are established from production control/data flow; I did not add or compile new reproductions. The existing tests cover individual cancellation/refresh/vault failures but not the reported overlapping-generation and crash cases.",
    "Retained current-input results show 91 frontend, 31 core-library, 15 Academy identity, 3 browser-callback, 12 IPC, 44 context and 17 scan tests passing. The targeted 56 frontend tests overlap the 91-test total. Mutation scripts/results were inspected, not rerun in the reviewed checkout.",
    "The 99 learner procedure names match the pinned Academy allowlist. All 12 required native checks are present and recorded passing against the supplied fixture executable. I inspected the native records and drivers without independently launching the GUI. Browser approval is simulated and the fixture opener records the page instead of invoking the production browser; spoken VoiceOver output is not recorded.",
    "D028 is an implementation choice under review, not evidence of hosted OAuth qualification. The identity provider and Academy are synthetic fixtures; actual Academy/Clerk configuration and live behavior remain C25. The new learner provider/link have no production learner-screen consumer until C05, and hosted-content performance budgets are preregistered for that later workload rather than measured here.",
    "No application source was changed, no product endpoints were called and no real credentials were accessed. This failing C04 verdict does not authorize advancing the implementation gate."
  ],
